questions.question: What is the infimum of a set $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$?
options: The smallest upper bound of $E$
Any element of $E$
The largest element of $E$
The greatest lower bound of $E$

questions.question: Which two properties characterise $m=\inf E$?
options: $m$ is the greatest lower bound of $E$.
$m\in E$ and $m$ is the smallest element
$m$ is an upper bound that is the least such
$m$ is simply any lower bound of $E$

questions.question: What is $\inf(0,1)$?
What is $\inf\{x\in\mathbb{R}\colon x \gt 2\}$?
options: $+\infty$

questions.question: Why can a set have an infimum without attaining it?
options: The infimum is always a limit point, and those lie outside the set.
Only infinite sets have an infimum, and it is never one of the elements.
A lower bound must lie strictly below every element of the set.
The infimum is a greatest lower bound, not necessarily in the set.

questions.question: How does the infimum of a set differ from its minimum?
options: A minimum must belong to the set, while an infimum need not
They coincide for every non-empty set that is bounded below
An infimum must belong to the set, while a minimum need not
Every bounded-below set has a minimum, but not always an infimum

questions.question: Let $A=\{x\in\mathbb{Q}\colon-\sqrt{2}<x\le\sqrt{2}\}$. What are $\inf A$ and $\max A$?
options: $\inf A$ does not exist, and neither does $\max A$.
$\inf A=-\sqrt{2}$, and $\max A$ does not exist.
$\inf A=-\sqrt{2}$, and $\max A=\sqrt{2}$.
$\inf A$ does not exist, and $\max A=\sqrt{2}$.

questions.question: For $E = \{x\in\mathbb{R}\colon x \gt 2\}$, which statement explains why $2$ is the infimum?
options: $2$ is the largest element of $E$.
$2$ is the greatest lower bound of $E$.
$2$ is not a lower bound of $E$.
$2$ is greater than every element of $E$.

questions.question: What value is assigned to $\inf E$ when $E$ is a nonempty subset of $\mathbb{R}$ with no lower bound?
options: $+\infty$
$-\infty$

questions.question: Why is the convention $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$ consistent with lower-bound language?
options: The empty set contains $+\infty$.
The empty set has a smallest real element.
$+\infty$ is a real number.
Every real is vacuously a lower bound of $\varnothing$.

questions.question: Give an example of an infimum that is not attained by the set.
Which conclusion follows from $m = \inf E$ for a nonempty set $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ that is bounded below?
options: $m$ is a lower bound of $E$; no larger one exists.
$m$ is a lower bound of $E$; no smaller one exists.
$m$ is the smallest element of $E$, so $m\in E$.
$m$ is strictly less than every element of $E$.

questions.question: For a nonempty set $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, what condition makes a real number a lower bound for $E$?
options: A number greater than or equal to every element of $E$
An element of $E$ that is less than or equal to all others
A number less than or equal to every element of $E$
A number less than or equal to some element of $E$

questions.question: Why is the infimum of a set called its greatest lower bound?
options: It is the smallest element, so it always belongs to the set.
It is the largest number strictly below every element.
It is a lower bound, and all others are no larger.
It is an upper bound, and all other upper bounds are larger.

questions.question: If $m=\inf E$, what does every choice of $\varepsilon>0$ guarantee?
options: Some element of $E$ is smaller than $m+\varepsilon$
Every element of $E$ is smaller than $m+\varepsilon$
$m+\varepsilon$ belongs to $E$
$E$ must be finite

questions.question: What is the infimum of a non-empty finite set of real numbers?
options: Its smallest element
Its largest element
Its element closest to $0$
None; it has a minimum instead

questions.question: What is $\inf\{1,2,3\}$?
Which real sets are guaranteed to have an infimum in $\mathbb{R}$?
options: Every non-empty set that is bounded below
Every set that is bounded below, even the empty set
Only closed sets that are bounded below
Every non-empty set, bounded below or not

questions.question: Why is the infimum unique?
options: Two greatest lower bounds must be equal.
A set can have no lower bounds
Every set has exactly one element
The infimum is chosen by convention only.

questions.question: For a non-empty set $E$, how do $\inf E$ and $\sup E$ compare?
options: $\inf E\le\sup E$
$\inf E>\sup E$
$\inf E=\sup E$ always
they cannot be compared
